concerns.text: The validation of neural alignment (H2) relies on a Phase‑Locking Value (PLV) computed between the model’s phase (which is directly generated by the injected sinusoidal mask) and human MEG phase. Because the model’s phase is a deterministic sinusoid at the target frequency, any non‑zero oscillatory mask will trivially increase PLV relative to the non‑oscillatory baseline, making the PLV outcome a direct function of the predictor. This creates a circular validation: the metric used to claim alignment is not independent of the intervention, so the test can never falsify the hypothesis and will always appear significant.

Hypothesis H2 states that PLV will be higher than baseline with p < 0.05. Since the baseline model lacks any oscillatory component, its PLV is effectively zero, while the oscillatory model’s PLV is guaranteed to be > 0 by construction. This makes the hypothesis trivially true and non‑empirical; the analysis cannot distinguish genuine neural similarity from the mere presence of a sinusoidal mask.

concerns.location: plan.md:Mapping of token processing time to physical time (Section 'Computational Neuro‑Biological Fidelity')
concerns.text: The plan assumes a fixed token‑to‑time conversion (≈10 ms per token) to map the relative frequency of the sinusoidal mask to a physical 40 Hz gamma band. This mapping is not empirically justified for the transformer architecture and introduces an arbitrary scaling factor, undermining the validity of comparing model frequencies to human MEG frequencies.
